topic: real usage entry attempt: external speech -> microphone -> system -> speaker
result: blocked by a microphone hardware fault; no speech amplification could be observed

attempts.note: ref = mic - 15 dB confirms the system did play the microphone signal
operator reported pure white noise plus faint howling: the loop was amplifying its own noise floor because no voice reached the microphone

microphone_check.command: direct capture, gain 0, loop open, 1-frame silent source, 8 s
microphone_check.operator_action: spoke loudly within about 10-20 cm of the microphone for 8 s
microphone_check.verdict: MIC_DEAD: the microphone level did not move while the operator spoke

timeline: the microphone worked at 2026-10-24 during the recalibration (mic -18.1 dBFS) and during the gate-drift test (-29 to -34 dBFS for the tones). It failed afterwards, around the 0 dB candidate saturation event.
explains: C's c-room-ready-v1 speech runs stopped at gate_tone_not_observed: the gate tone could not be seen by a microphone that was no longer working
both speech attempts heard only amplified noise and a faint howl, never the operator's voice
next: operator reseats VCC / GND / LINE_IN or swaps the MAX4466 module, then the same 8 s microphone check decides whether it is serviceable
consequence_for_results: no conclusion about speech amplification can be drawn from this round; the earlier closed-loop trials that the package accepted are unaffected because they used digital injection
microphone_status: recovered. The module was not damaged: the VCC/GND/LINE_IN wiring was loose. After reseating, an 8 s speech check read mic -11.9 dBFS with 14 full-scale samples, i.e. alive and very hot.

speech_trials_after_repair.operator: white noise dominated plus faint sharp howling
quieter than before, only hiss, no voice

root_cause_of_the_audible_noise: with bypass the played signal is gain*microphone. At -9 dB the loop gain is |H|-9 dB and the fixture's |H| reaches +5..+11 dB near 8.4 kHz, so the loop sits at the edge: the microphone noise floor is boosted by 1/(1-gH) (audible hiss) and individual bins cross unity (the sharp howl).
why_no_amplification_is_audible: bypass at a negative gain plays the voice quieter than the voice itself, so it can never sound amplified. Audible amplification requires gain at or above 0 dB, and at 0 dB bypass is unstable on this fixture because |H| exceeds 0 dB near 8.4 kHz. Cancellation is what has to buy that range, and the current model only holds to about -3 dB.
conclusion: the real usage entry (external speech -> microphone -> system -> speaker) is NOT yet demonstrated. The hardware path works end to end (the system plays the microphone signal, verified by ref = mic - gain at both gains), but no gain that would be audible as amplification is stable.
gap: at least 3 dB and up to 9 dB of loop-gain margin at the 8.4 kHz resonance, depending on which session's H applies; the fixture's own 4.7 dB repeatability is the same size as the gap, so the margin cannot be closed by measurement alone.
